**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Docs-only PR (3 files under `site/content/guide/`): no Rust, no build.rs, no `.github/`, no scripts, no process files, no dependencies, no snapshot PNGs, no CHANGELOG edit. PROCESS_VERSION bump not needed.

**What looks good**
- Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn sections follow the Wire Contour shape (what it is for, settings by tab with seed defaults, picks, refusals).
- I spot-checked the quoted refusals against source and they match: `tools/src/electrode.rs` (spindle, Y size, sharp-cornered), `motion/src/sinker.rs` (burns nothing, would never enter the work, holder would enter the work), `motion/src/sinker_side.rs` (moves no wall, exceeds the electrode undersize, takes no orbit), `app/src/operation/sinker_op.rs` (no maximum orbit radius), `app/src/posting_family.rs` (no post for a sinker EDM machine yet), `app/src/stock_sim.rs` (no sinker electrode atom). Side-burn seed defaults 0.1 / 0.2 mm match `sinker_side_op.rs`.
- The stale "sinker EDM kind admits no operation yet" sentence in machines.md is fixed, and the operations.md row and link text are consistent.
- Honest about the post status (#542) and the stock view gap; no clean-room concerns (own words, quoted from our source).
- Body has `Changelog: none`, `Refs #1250` (partial work, does not close), conventional subject.

**Local results (merged with main, trial merge clean)**
- Build / cargo tests / clippy: not applicable, no code touched.
- zola build: not re-run here (zola is not installed on this reviewer machine); the author reports 42 pages, 0 orphans, and the `#sinker-edm` anchor in the diff is a plain heading anchor. Read the diff in full instead.

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `operations.md` line about "the multi-axis kinds, Probe, Plasma Profile and the EDM kinds..." now runs past the file's usual wrap width; cosmetic.
- The "Z axis: required for a sinker EDM machine" message is quoted from a formatted string I could not find as a literal; it is presumably built from the kind name. Worth a glance by whoever knows that code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
